summary: This article explains how rowing crews use an oar's leverage, careful timing, and teamwork to move a narrow boat quickly through water.
introduce: Start a K-W-L chart on the board and ask students what they already Know and what they Want to know about the topic of “Rowing: Power in a Boat”. Tell them they will fill in what they Learned after reading.

keyTerms.def: a group of people who work together to operate a boat
the person who steers a rowing boat and calls out the rhythm for the rowers
the force that keeps a moving object going in the same direction

challengeTerms.def: a simple machine, often a rigid bar, that turns around a fixed point to move or lift something
one complete cycle of movement, such as pulling an oar through the water and lifting it out again
happening at exactly the same time as something else, in a coordinated way

discussion: Do you agree or disagree that teamwork matters more than individual strength in sports? Use evidence from the article to explain.
Explain how timing and coordination affect a rowing crew's speed.
struggling: Read the first part of the article aloud together, review crew, coxswain, and momentum, and let weak readers use a K-W-L chart and read the article with a partner.
gifted: Challenge advanced readers to use lever, stroke, and synchronized in a short paragraph that connects the article to something they learned in another subject.
